steps.name: Additive 0011 migration creates the instance_admins role table
criteria: Applying the canonical forward-only migration set (0009, 0010, 0011) against a pre-feature schema succeeds and yields an instance_admins table keyed on user_id as primary key
The 0011 migration adds no column to and rewrites no row of any prior table; it only creates the new empty instance_admins table
Re-applying the full migration set a second time neither errors nor duplicates the instance_admins table (IF NOT EXISTS idempotence)
No migration file numbered 0001 through 0010 is modified by this step (forward-only discipline)
The newly created instance_admins table is empty until a super-admin is seeded
steps.scenario_name: Re-running the upgrade does not duplicate or alter anything

steps.name: is_instance_admin authz predicate in store and services
criteria: Given a user whose id is present in instance_admins, an instance-admin check for that user returns true
Given a user whose id is absent from instance_admins, the check returns false (fail-closed: absence denies)
The instance-admin check takes only a user identity and no workspace argument, so it is instance-scoped and never tenant-scoped
The check mirrors the shipped is_workspace_admin EXISTS shape and resolves with a single existence query
An empty instance_admins table denies every user (no implicit super-admin)
steps.scenario_name: A non-super-admin cannot provision a workspace

steps.name: Bootstrap claim seeds the operator as first super-admin
criteria: When an operator claims the instance at bootstrap (creating workspace 1 and its admin), that operator is also recorded as the first instance_admins row in the same atomic claim
The bootstrap-claiming operator is both workspace 1's admin and the first super-admin with no separate instance identity
After the claim, the bootstrap-claiming operator passes the instance-admin authz check and can provision a new workspace
A fresh instance never exists with a workspace 1 but no provisioning authority
Seeding the first super-admin touches no existing tenant data beyond inserting the single instance_admins row
steps.scenario_name: The bootstrap-claiming operator is the first super-admin and can provision

steps.name: grant-super-admin CLI is idempotent for upgraded installs
criteria: On an upgraded install with workspace Acme and no super-admin yet, running the grant-super-admin command for the operator records exactly one instance_admins row
Running grant-super-admin a second time for the same operator records the grant exactly once (idempotent ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING semantics)
After being granted, the operator passes the instance-admin authz check and can then provision a new workspace
The grant subcommand is reachable only from the operator CLI and never from the bearer API surface
Granting super-admin alters no existing tenant data beyond the single instance_admins insert
steps.scenario_name: An upgraded install grants its first super-admin and can then provision

phases.name: CLI provisioning surface + provisioned-tenant isolation proof (D2)

steps.name: provision-workspace CLI happy path creates a real isolated tenant
criteria: When a super-admin runs the provision-workspace command with a workspace name and a first-admin email, a new workspace is created and isolated from all existing workspaces
The command reports the new workspace identity and a first-admin invite link on its output
The seeded first admin signs in, lands on the new workspace, and acts on it through the shipped sign-in and active-workspace resolution seam
Provisioning is invoked as a real operator CLI subprocess against a real database, never as a direct internal use-case call
The new workspace and its first admin are created atomically, mirroring the shipped initial-workspace seeding transaction
steps.scenario_name: A super-admin provisions a new isolated workspace with a first admin

steps.name: Provisioning a new workspace leaves existing workspaces untouched
criteria: When a super-admin provisions a new workspace, the only rows inserted belong to that new workspace and its first admin
Every pre-existing workspace's rows are unchanged row-for-row after provisioning, compared against a before-snapshot of those workspaces
The newly provisioned workspace's identity is distinct from every existing workspace identity
Provisioning performs no cross-write, update, or delete into any existing tenant's rows
The new-tenant insert and the existing-tenant invariance are both proven against a real database, not by inspecting internal call paths
steps.scenario_name: Provisioning a new workspace leaves existing workspaces untouched

steps.name: Provisioned workspace honors the shipped isolation boundary
criteria: After a super-admin provisions a new workspace with issues belonging to it, the new workspace's admin listing her issues sees only that workspace's issues
No existing-workspace issue appears in the provisioned tenant's scoped reads
No provisioned-tenant issue appears in any existing workspace's scoped reads
Isolation is proven green-by-inheritance through the shipped scoped-read ports without new isolation code
The provisioned workspace is a real coexisting tenant resolved through the same shipped active-workspace seam as workspace 1
steps.scenario_name: The provisioned workspace is a real coexisting tenant that sees only its own data

steps.name: Cross-tenant reach into the provisioned workspace is non-enumerable
criteria: When a member of the existing workspace requests a real provisioned-tenant resource by its real address, the response is refused
When that same member requests a resource that never existed, the response is refused identically to the real-but-foreign request
The two refusals are observationally indistinguishable, so the refusal reveals nothing about whether the provisioned tenant or its resource exists
The cross-tenant refusal reuses the shipped uniform-404 idiom and exposes no 403-versus-404 existence oracle
No provisioned-tenant data crosses into the existing-workspace member's response under either request
steps.scenario_name: A member of the existing workspace cannot reach the provisioned one non-enumerably

steps.name: Provisioning authz refusal is fail-closed and non-enumerable
criteria: When a regular member who is not a super-admin attempts to provision a workspace, the attempt is refused as not authorized via a distinct structured non-zero CLI exit code
After an unauthorized attempt, no new workspace was created
An unauthorized attempt against a name matching an existing workspace and against a name that never existed are refused identically
Neither refusal reveals whether the target workspace already exists (no existence oracle; refusal is observationally independent of target existence)
The authz gate denies before any workspace lookup so refusal carries no information about target state
steps.scenario_name: An unauthorized provisioning attempt does not reveal whether the target exists

steps.name: Provisioning is unreachable from the bearer API surface
criteria: When a caller uses a machine token bound to a workspace to attempt provisioning over the /api/v1 bearer surface, no provisioning path is reachable
After the bearer-surface attempt, no new workspace was created
Provisioning remains exclusively on the operator CLI surface (api differs from mint), preserving the shipped verify-path-unchanged invariant
Even a workspace-1-bound machine token cannot reach any provisioning endpoint
steps.scenario_name: Provisioning is unreachable from the bearer API surface

steps.name: Existing single-workspace install upgrades and resolves to workspace 1
criteria: When a real pre-feature single-workspace install is upgraded to multi-workspace support, the existing workspace becomes the first workspace with its identity unchanged
All of the upgraded workspace's tenant data is present and unchanged after the upgrade
A user whose active workspace was never chosen resolves to the first workspace via the shipped NULL-active plus sole-membership resolution path
The upgrade is driven through the same migration runner the production boot path uses (0009, 0010, 0011 applied forward-only)
The upgrade is the walking skeleton for slice 5: it proves the end-to-end migration-then-resolve path before the finer guarantees are split out
steps.scenario_name: Upgrading a single-workspace install keeps it working as workspace 1

steps.name: Real-snapshot before/after equality proves rows are untouched
criteria: Given a recorded snapshot of every tenant table before the upgrade, after the upgrade every tenant row is present and unchanged when compared row-for-row against the snapshot
The existing workspace's identity is unchanged across the upgrade
The before/after snapshot harness is a new DELIVER prerequisite authored to capture and diff every tenant table against a real database before the assertion runs
The guarantee is achieved by before/after-equality proof against a real database, not by rewriting any row
No row is rewritten, backfilled, or re-keyed by the upgrade (the equality proof would fail on any rewrite)
steps.scenario_name: No tenant data is lost or changed by the upgrade

steps.name: Carried sessions and machine tokens still resolve after the upgrade
criteria: A session created before the upgrade still resolves to and acts on the first workspace afterward
A valid machine token created before the upgrade still resolves to and acts on the first workspace afterward
The carried credentials require no re-issue or re-binding to keep working across the upgrade
Credential resolution after the upgrade flows through the shipped active-workspace resolution seam unchanged
steps.scenario_name: Existing sessions and machine tokens still resolve after the upgrade

steps.name: Upgraded user resolves to workspace 1 without writing active workspace
criteria: An upgraded user who never chose an active workspace resolves to the first workspace via the shipped NULL-active plus sole-membership resolution path
After resolution, the user's active_workspace_id remains unwritten and NULL (observable proof of the no-backfill decision D4)
Resolution to the first workspace writes no row and performs no backfill update on the user or membership tables
Re-resolving the same user repeatedly continues to yield the first workspace while active_workspace_id stays NULL
The unwritten active-workspace state is verified against a real database, not inferred from internal resolution code
steps.scenario_name: An upgraded user resolves to workspace 1 without their active workspace being written

steps.name: Existing sign-in and workspace behaviour is unchanged after the upgrade
criteria: An existing member signs in after the upgrade and lands on the first workspace
After sign-in the member sees exactly the issues and projects they saw before the upgrade, with nothing added or removed
No behavioural change is observable at the sign-in or web surface compared with the pre-upgrade single-workspace experience
The single-workspace experience is preserved as the one-membership special case of multi-workspace, not a separate code path
The unchanged behaviour is proven through the shipped sign-in and scoped-read seams, not by inspecting internals
steps.scenario_name: Existing sign-in and workspace behaviour is unchanged after the upgrade

steps.name: Idle plus LRU size-cap eviction bounds the RevokeRateLimiter map
criteria: Advancing the shipped clock past the idle window (W = ceil(C/R) seconds) evicts buckets idle beyond W, bounding the in-memory map under many idle principals
An active principal's throttle decision is byte-identical with eviction enabled and disabled (idle eviction is behaviour-preserving)
Under pathological load the LRU size-cap fallback bounds the map by size and only ever under-throttles, never over-throttling an active principal (one-directional relaxation)
Eviction reads the existing clock seam and introduces zero new crate (std HashMap retain only)
Eviction is exercised by MockClock-driven unit and property tests at the rate-limit module, not by an HTTP acceptance scenario
steps.scenario_name: rate_limit::tests (MockClock-driven idle-eviction and LRU size-cap unit/property tests)
